---
format:
  typst:
    paper: a4
---

```{=typst}
// ── Palette and fonts ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#let accent = rgb("#1F4E5F")
#let body-font  = ("Source Serif 4", "New Computer Modern", "Georgia")
#let label-font = ("Source Sans 3", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial")
#let muted = luma(105)

#set page(
  margin: (x: 2.0cm, y: 1.9cm),
  footer: context [
    #set text(font: label-font, size: 8pt, fill: luma(120))
    #grid(
      columns: (1fr, auto, 1fr),
      align(left)[Aske Halling · Curriculum Vitae],
      align(center)[#counter(page).display()],
      align(right)[#emph[Updated September 2026]]
    )
  ]
)
#set text(font: body-font, size: 10.5pt, lang: "en")
#set par(leading: 0.64em, justify: false)
#show link: set text(fill: accent)

// ── Building blocks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Margin label: sans-serif, small, letterspaced (section headings, years, status)
#let lbl(body) = text(font: label-font, size: 8pt, weight: "semibold",
                      fill: muted, tracking: 0.9pt)[#upper[#body]]
#let side(body) = text(font: label-font, size: 9pt, fill: muted)[#body]

// Section: heading hangs in the left margin, content in the text column
#let section(title, body) = {
  grid(
    columns: (2.9cm, 1fr),
    column-gutter: 0.6cm,
    align(top)[#lbl(title)],
    body
  )
}

// Rows of (left-column label, content). Left column holds years or status.
#let rows(items) = grid(
  columns: (1.8cm, 1fr),
  column-gutter: 0.42cm,
  row-gutter: 0.30cm,
  ..items.map(p => (align(top + left)[#side(p.at(0))], p.at(1))).flatten()
)

// Position / degree: bold title over italic affiliation
#let role(title, org) = [
  *#title* \
  #text(style: "italic", fill: luma(85))[#org]
]

#let au = [Department of Political Science, Aarhus University]

// Spacing: between sections inside a block, and between blocks
#let gap = v(0.62cm)
#let blockgap = v(1.05cm)

// ── Header: name left, contact right, rule across the full measure ───────────
#grid(
  columns: (1fr, auto),
  column-gutter: 0.8cm,
  align: bottom,
  [
    #text(size: 22pt, weight: "regular", fill: accent)[Aske Halling]
    #h(5pt)
    #text(size: 10.5pt, fill: luma(120), style: "italic")[PhD]
  ],
  align(right + bottom)[
    #text(size: 9.5pt, fill: luma(70))[
      #link("mailto:aske@ps.au.dk")[aske\@ps.au.dk]
      #h(0.5em) #text(fill: luma(190))[|] #h(0.5em)
      #link("https://askehalling.com")[askehalling.com]
      #h(0.5em) #text(fill: luma(190))[|] #h(0.5em)
      #link("https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=AyPnunoAAAAJ&hl=en")[scholar.google.com]
    ]
  ]
)
#v(0.28cm)
#line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.8pt + accent)
#v(0.7cm)

// ── Block 1: position and education ──────────────────────────────────────────
#section("Current Employment")[
  #rows((
    ("2023–", role("Assistant Professor", au)),
  ))
]
#gap

#section("University Education")[
  #rows((
    ("2023", role("PhD in Political Science", au)),
    ("2018", role("Master's degree in Political Science (MSc)", au)),
    ("2016", role("Bachelor's degree in Political Science (BA)", au)),
  ))
]
#gap

#section("Foreign University Stays")[
  #rows((
    ("2021", [Research stay, KU Leuven]),
  ))
]
#blockgap

// ── Block 2: research output ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
// Year shown only on the first publication of each year
#section("Publications")[
  #rows((
    ("2026", [Burden Without Backlash? Trust and Procedural Fairness in Response to Welfare Compliance Demands (with Frederik Godt). Conditionally accepted in _Policy Studies Journal_.]),
    ("", [Beyond the Hassle: How Favorable Outcomes Reduce the Subjective Experience of Administrative Burden (with Frederik Godt). _International Public Management Journal_.]),
    ("", [Do Justifications Affect Tolerance for Administrative Burdens? Evidence from a Survey-Experiment Among Policy Makers (with Steven van de Walle). _Social Policy and Administration_ 60(1): 12–26.]),
    ("", [Acceptable or Not? Understanding Attitudes Toward Citizens' Discrimination Against Frontline Workers (with Mathilde Cecchini and Benedicte Gronhoj). _Public Administration_ 104(3): 459–475.]),
    ("2025", [Taxing Language: Do Interpreting Fees Affect Immigrant Healthcare Usage? Evidence from a Regression Discontinuity Design. _Public Administration Review_ 85(4): 1019–1037.]),
    ("", [Deservingness at the Frontline: How Health-related Responsibility Cues Affect Sanctioning and Prioritization of Citizens (with Julian Christensen, Frederik Godt Hansen, and Niels Bjørn Grund Petersen). _Public Administration_ 103(1): 94–114.]),
    ("", [Burden Tolerance: Developing a Validated Measurement Instrument across Seven Countries (with Martin Bækgaard and Donald Moynihan). _Public Administration Review_ 85(2): 519–546.]),
    ("2024", [Administrative byrder i mødet med lægen: oplevelser af efterlevelsesomkostninger blandt borgere med dårligt helbred. _Politica_ 56(4): 318–336.]),
    ("", [Frontline Employees' Responses to Citizens' Communication of Administrative Burdens (with Niels Bjørn Grund Petersen). _Public Administration Review_ 84(6): 1017–1037.]),
    ("", [Administrative Burden in Citizen-State Interactions: A Systematic Literature Review (with Martin Bækgaard). _Journal of Public Administration Research and Theory_ 34(2): 180–195.]),
    ("2023", [How Difficult Should It Be? Evidence of Burden Tolerance from a Nationally Representative Sample (with Pamela Herd and Donald Moynihan). _Public Management Review_ 25(11): 2053–2072.]),
  ))
]
#gap

    ("R&R", [No evidence of ethnic discrimination in Danish caseworkers' sanctioning intentions: a high-powered, preregistered survey experiment (with Julian Christensen, Frederik Godt, and Niels Bjørn Grund Petersen). _Journal of Behavioral Public Administration_.]),
    ("R&R", [Færre valgsteder, færre vælgere? Valgstedslukninger og valgdeltagelse fra 2007-2026 (with Lea Munksgaard Rubin). _Politica_.]),
    ("In progress", [Personality as a Mechanism of Inequality in Experiences of Administrative Burdens.]),
    ("In progress", ["Everybody Should Be Able to Attend to Any Client, But…" – How Frontline Workers and Frontline Managers Interpret Citizens' Differential Treatment of Staff (with Mathilde Cecchini and Benedicte Gronhoj).]),
    ("In progress", [How Representative Are Politically Active Social Media Users? A Descriptive Large-Scale Study of Danish Twitter Users (with Michael Bang Petersen and Stig Hebbelstrup Rye Rasmussen).]),
    ("In progress", [Deservingness Perceptions and Burden Tolerance: A Conjoint Experiment.]),

  ))
```
